overview: EverCommerce is a Denver-based provider of integrated, vertically-tailored SaaS solutions for service-based small and medium-sized businesses ("service SMBs"), serving more than 745,000 customers across three core verticals: EverPro (Home Services), EverHealth (Health Services) and EverWell (Wellness Services). The company pairs business-management software (the customer's system of action) with embedded billing/payment processing and customer-experience tools, monetizing through recurring subscription fees plus payment take-rate on roughly $13 billion of annualized processing volume. In October 2025, EverCommerce sold its marketing technology solutions business to Ignite Visibility, narrowing the company to its core vertical-SaaS-plus-payments model and lifting reported gross margin from the low-60s% to the mid-70s% purely as a mix effect, not an operating improvement.

business_model.summary: Land-and-expand vertical SaaS: a vertically-tailored Business Management Software product is typically the first solution sold to a customer, after which EverCommerce cross-sells integrated payments (the largest margin-expansion lever), billing/invoicing automation and customer-experience/AI tools. Revenue is split into Subscription and Transaction Fees (~96% of revenue, recurring/re-occurring) and Other (one-time services, hardware, implementation). Roughly 93% of customers generate under $2,000/year in revenue, reflecting a long-tail SMB base; growth since 2017 has come through 54 acquisitions as well as organic cross-sell.

revenue_streams.name: Subscription and transaction fees (SaaS + integrated payments)
Other (professional services, hardware, website dev, partnerships)

business_model.customer_type: B2B / SMB — predominantly owner-operated service businesses (home improvement contractors, physician/therapy practices, salons/spas); ~68% US, ~32% international (Canada, UK, Australia, New Zealand)
business_model.geographic_mix: United States ~68% of customers, international ~32% (Canada, UK, Australia, New Zealand)

competitive_position.market_position: One of the few at-scale, multi-vertical SMB software platforms spanning home services, health services and wellness; management estimates a $1.6 trillion global TAM (~$662 billion in North America) that remains largely untapped. Faces newer, better-funded, vertically-focused challengers (e.g., ServiceTitan in home services) that are growing faster in their single vertical, while EverCommerce's breadth is both a diversification benefit and a dilution of focus.

moat_factors.description: Business Management Software becomes the customer's system of record for scheduling, dispatch, invoicing and records, creating data and workflow lock-in that is costly for a small operator to migrate away from.

Once payments are embedded into the software, switching requires re-platforming both workflow and money movement; payments also improve EverCommerce's own unit economics and margin as attach rates rise.

Purpose-built workflows for narrow micro-verticals (HVAC, pest control, med-aesthetics, behavioral health, etc.) are harder for horizontal platforms (Salesforce, Intuit) to replicate cost-effectively.
54 acquisitions since inception give EverCommerce a repeatable integration playbook and sourcing network, though pace of M&A has slowed materially since 2022.

No single EverCommerce-branded product is a clear category leader the way ServiceTitan, Jobber or Mindbody are within their own single vertical; EverCommerce's advantage is breadth across verticals, not depth/leadership within any one.

weaknesses: No dominant, singular brand — a multi-vertical "roll-up" structure recognized by multiple sub-brands (EverPro, EverHealth, EverWell) rather than one platform with network effects
Net revenue retention has deteriorated from ~97% to ~93% year-over-year (Q3 2026), signaling rising churn/contraction or weaker cross-sell execution
Organic new-customer acquisition has slowed (fewer leads via organic search), and revenue growth has decelerated from high-single-digit pro forma growth to ~2-3%
Highly fragmented, low-differentiation long tail of micro-vertical competitors with low switching costs for the smallest customers
Unremediated material weakness in internal control over financial reporting (order-to-cash revenue processes) first identified in FY2023 and still open as of Q3 2026

"Controlled company" governance structure (Providence Strategic Growth and other sponsor stockholders hold a CEO-approval veto right), which is also the subject of ongoing Delaware Chancery Court litigation

growth_drivers: Payments penetration: cross-selling integrated payments into the existing SaaS base is management's primary lever for ARPU and margin expansion (estimated >$100 billion aggregate annualized payments opportunity vs. ~$13 billion processed today)

Cross-sell/up-sell of adjacent Customer Experience and AI solutions (e.g., ZyraTalk agentic AI assistant, acquired September 2025) into the EverPro home-services base, with plans to extend into EverHealth and EverWell
New product/micro-vertical expansion funded by a disciplined, selective M&A strategy (54 deals since 2017, though pace has slowed sharply since 2022)
Secular SMB digitization tailwinds: digital payment adoption among SMBs has risen from <50% to ~80% in recent years; continued shift from manual/legacy tools to integrated SaaS

New CEO (Alex Goor, effective August 2026) pursuing a strategy shift toward targeted paid-media/product-led growth aimed at reaccelerating revenue growth, though management itself has pushed the reacceleration timeline out to late 2027
Capital return: an expanded $325 million cumulative share-repurchase authorization (through December 2027) funded by free cash flow, with $28.5 million remaining as of Q3 2026

business.description: Pro forma revenue growth fell from ~8.5% (FY2024) to ~2.1-2.4% (Q3 2026), and annualized net revenue retention declined from ~97% to ~93% year-over-year, suggesting weakening demand, slower new-logo adds (fewer organic search leads) and/or rising customer attrition.

Faces vertically-focused, well-funded competitors (ServiceTitan, Jobber, Mindbody, Zenoti) that out-grow EverCommerce within single verticals, plus horizontal players (Salesforce, Intuit, Square) and low-cost manual/point solutions long-tail SMBs can default to.

business.risk: Customer concentration in very small accounts
business.description: ~93% of customers contribute under $2,000/year in revenue; this long-tail base is price-sensitive and prone to closure/churn in economic downturns.

Founder-CEO Eric Remer stepped down in August 2026, replaced by external hire Alex Goor; new strategy (shift to paid media/PLG) has already resulted in a guidance cut and a reacceleration timeline pushed to late 2027, with associated one-time severance/equity acceleration costs.

Business built via 54 acquisitions; recently divested marketing technology (Oct 2025) and Fitness Solutions (2024), and may continue to prune non-core assets — execution risk cuts both ways on growth and on further portfolio simplification.

financial.description: ~$522.5 million outstanding on a Term Loan (effective rate ~6.09%) against ~$180 million Adjusted EBITDA (FY2025); leverage constrains capital flexibility despite 2025 refinancing that extended maturities to 2030/2031 and reduced margins.
A material weakness in internal control over order-to-cash revenue processes, identified as of December 31, 2023, remains unremediated as of Q3 2026, creating restatement/reporting risk.
Partially hedged via interest rate swaps on the Term Loan; modest foreign-currency exposure from ~32% international customer base (Canada, UK, Australia, NZ).

regulatory.description: Dependent on Visa/Mastercard and processors/sponsors (Worldpay, PayPal); non-compliance can trigger fines, suspension or termination of payment registrations.
HIPAA and other healthcare privacy/billing regulations apply directly and through customers in the Health Services vertical.

Exposure to an expanding patchwork of US state privacy/AI laws (CCPA, Colorado AI Act, Utah AI Policy Act) and the EU AI Act (substantive provisions effective August 2026) as the company embeds generative/agentic AI (e.g., ZyraTalk) into its products.
Ongoing Delaware Chancery Court litigation (Vladimir Gusinsky Revocable Trust) challenging the Sponsor Stockholders' CEO-approval veto right under the sponsor stockholders' agreement.

macro.description: Revenue is directly tied to the health, spending, and survival of small/medium service businesses; a weakening economy could cause higher SMB closures, reduced transaction volumes and pricing pressure, each of which flows directly through recurring subscription and payments revenue.

End-consumer demand for home improvement, wellness/salon and elective health services (which drive EverCommerce customers' own revenue, and therefore EverCommerce's transaction volumes) is cyclical and discretionary.
Management flags tariff uncertainty, inflation and interest-rate volatility as macro factors that could affect SMB customers' capital spending on software and EverCommerce's own borrowing costs.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Vertical SaaS and embedded payments for SMBs remains an early-innings, large and underpenetrated market (management-estimated $1.6 trillion global TAM, ~$662 billion in North America) with digital-payments and AI-adoption tailwinds, but competitive intensity has increased sharply as better-capitalized, single-vertical players (e.g., ServiceTitan) scale faster than diversified multi-vertical platforms.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — revenue is largely recurring/subscription-based (~96-97%), which cushions cyclicality, but the underlying customer base (small service businesses) and payment transaction volumes are exposed to SMB formation/closure rates and consumer discretionary spending cycles.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — ~$522.5 million variable-rate Term Loan (partially swapped to fixed) means borrowing costs move with SOFR; higher rates also indirectly pressure SMB customers' capital spending decisions.

recent_developments.event: Completed sale of the marketing technology solutions business to Ignite Visibility for ~$45 million cash, reported as discontinued operations; narrows the company to core vertical-SaaS-plus-payments model and structurally lifts reported gross margin (mix effect, not operating improvement).

Acquired Joblyt LLC (dba ZyraTalk), an AI-powered virtual-assistant/agentic-automation platform, for ~$36 million cash plus up to $6.5 million contingent consideration, to accelerate AI-driven customer engagement starting in the Home Services (EverPro) vertical.

Founder and CEO Eric Remer stepped down (remains a board member); external hire Alex Goor (20+ years fintech/technology leadership, ex-ACA Compliance, Interactive Data, Instinet, Datek Online) appointed CEO effective August 6, 2026, alongside a Q2 2026 earnings report and a weaker-than-expected update.
ZyraTalk founders departed the company voluntarily during integration, forfeiting remaining earnout/retention compensation after receiving a $3.0 million payment.
Board increased the share-repurchase authorization by an additional $25 million, bringing cumulative authorization since 2022 to $325 million, extended through December 31, 2027.

Reported Q3 2026 results: revenue of $151.4 million (+2.7% YoY), Adjusted EBITDA of $45.0 million (down from $46.5 million YoY), annualized net revenue retention of ~93% (down from ~97% a year earlier); cut full-year 2026 guidance to roughly $600 million revenue / ~$170 million Adjusted EBITDA (from a prior $612-632 million / $183-191 million range) and said new CEO Alex Goor's strategy shift toward targeted paid media / product-led growth is expected to push revenue reacceleration out to late 2027; stock sold off sharply on the report.

items.notes: Cut from prior guidance of $612-632 million (set with Q2 2026 results in August 2026); management cited weaker organic lead generation, flat vendor-rebate expectations and incremental Q4 investment.
Cut from prior guidance of $183-191 million; implies a lower Adjusted EBITDA margin than FY2025's $180.5 million on higher revenue.
Down from ~97% in the prior-year quarter; management has not issued forward NRR guidance but flagged it as a continued area of focus under the new CEO's strategy.
New CEO's shift toward targeted paid media and product-led growth is framed as a multi-quarter initiative; management does not expect meaningful reacceleration before late 2027.

guidance.management_commentary: Management said its "outlook for the balance of 2026 has moderated" and that full-year results are now expected to track to the lower end of (and ultimately below) the previously communicated ranges. New CEO Alex Goor is repositioning go-to-market around paid-media-driven, product-led growth rather than organic search, with benefits not expected to show up materially in results until late 2027.

bull_case: Highly recurring revenue base (~96-97% subscription/transaction) with a large, underpenetrated TAM (~$662 billion North America, ~$1.6 trillion globally) and still-low integrated-payments penetration relative to a >$100 billion estimated payments opportunity
Payments cross-sell is a direct, high-margin lever that has already driven gross margin into the mid-70s% post-divestiture, with further room as attach rates rise across the ~745,000-customer base

Aggressive capital return: $325 million cumulative buyback authorization through 2027 at a depressed valuation (stock trading well below pre-Q3-2026-selloff levels) provides a floor and per-share value creation independent of top-line reacceleration

New external CEO (Alex Goor) brings fresh fintech/payments leadership and an explicit mandate to fix growth, with his incentive package reportedly tied to share-price hurdles ($10/$20), aligning management with shareholder upside
Simplified, more focused portfolio post-divestitures (marketing technology, Fitness Solutions) should make the remaining EverPro/EverHealth/EverWell core easier to operate and underwrite
bear_case: Growth has decelerated sharply (pro forma growth down to ~2% from high-single-digits in 2024) alongside falling net revenue retention (~93% vs. ~97% a year ago), and management itself has pushed meaningful reacceleration out to late 2027 — a long wait for investors

Guidance was cut twice within one earnings cycle (Q2 to Q3 2026), damaging credibility and signaling the business may be losing share to faster-growing, vertically-focused competitors (ServiceTitan, Jobber, Mindbody, Zenoti) within its own core verticals

CEO transition (founder Remer out, external hire Goor in) adds execution and strategy-continuity risk precisely when the business needs stabilization, with one-time severance/equity-acceleration costs already weighing on margins
Unremediated material weakness in internal controls over revenue recognition (open since FY2023) raises the risk of further restatements or reporting issues

SMB customer base is inherently more fragile in a weakening macro environment (closures, reduced transaction volumes, price sensitivity), and the company carries meaningful leverage (~$522.5 million term loan) against a shrinking Adjusted EBITDA growth trajectory
"Controlled company" governance (Sponsor Stockholders' CEO-approval veto) limits the board's independence and is the subject of ongoing Delaware Chancery Court litigation, adding governance overhang
